name: White Sox South Loop Ballpark Proposal at The 78
current_value: The proposal sought roughly $1B in Illinois state funding/financing support; the legislature did not act on it, and no subsidy has been secured. This is distinct from the Chicago Fire's stadium at the same site, which is privately financed by owner Joe Mansueto (reported at $650M-$750M; broke ground March 3, 2026, no taxpayer dollars).
proposed_value: The original $1B Illinois state-funding ask for a ballpark at The 78 remains dead (legislature never acted). Separately: on Aug 14, 2026 the federal government awarded Amtrak grants totaling roughly $572M-$696M (reported combined/rounded across outlets) to relocate Amtrak's South Loop maintenance facility to a Union Pacific yard in Bridgeport, with Ishbia's entity Canal Edge contributing $125M+ to accelerate that move. This frees the 47-acre South Loop rail yard the relocation vacates. No new public-subsidy dollar figure has been confirmed for a stadium itself.
note: 2-source-plus confirmed (Amtrak's own release + Crain's + Sun-Times + The Real Deal); the ~$572M vs ~$696M spread reflects different outlets combining different grant components, not a real disagreement -- a maintainer should check Amtrak's release for the authoritative breakdown before quoting a single figure. This is infrastructure financing that ENABLES a future stadium site, not a stadium subsidy itself -- do not fold it into announced_investment_usd.

name: White Sox South Loop Ballpark Proposal at The 78
current_value: ~$1 billion was the working public-private cost estimate for a standalone White Sox ballpark at The 78 when the ask went to Springfield in 2024-2025; that funding request failed to advance, stalling the plan. Independently confirmed via fresh searches: Sox Machine and Forbes both describe the 'estimated $1 billion stadium.' The 2024 partner-map figure of $4 billion does not match any ballpark-spec
proposed_value: On Sept 5, 2026, incoming owner Justin Ishbia's Canal Edge unveiled renderings for 'The Railyards' -- a proposed new stadium site directly across the Chicago River from The 78, on the South Loop rail yard freed up by the Aug 14, 2026 Amtrak relocation grant (see public_subsidy_note). This is an early-stage, unapproved proposal: reporting describes a 'months-long feasibility study' (transportation/environmental) just beginning, not a committed site or design. No total project cost was published -- coverage says only the district 'will be in the billions,' which is not a citable figure. This is a NEW site proposal, not a revival of the original $1B/The 78 ask, which remains dead.
note: 5-source confirmed (Sun-Times, ABC7, Urbanize Chicago, Chicago YIMBY, WGN). No dollar amount is proposed for announced_investment_usd -- none was published. Maintainer's call whether status_2026 should move off 'stalled' given a new site now has renderings and a feasibility study underway, versus staying 'stalled' because nothing is approved or funded yet; this sweep does not propose an enum change on that ambiguity.
